records.current_summary: The July 2026 national legal-risk assessment places Delaware in its “low-risk states” group — states that largely refrain from targeting transgender adults without specialising in their protection — and nothing in Delaware’s record rises above that description in either direction. A national equality tracker records no public-facility-use ban for Delaware, and a September 2026 status check likewise found no enacted facility ban, while flagging that the tracker’s own citation (a page since relocated) still awaits one manual re-verification.

prison_adds.title: Transgender legal history in the United States (Wikipedia)
prison_adds.summary: Wikipedia's survey of US transgender legal history documents the shifting federal framework for housing trans prisoners: a January 2015 ICE memo directed housing transgender immigration detainees according to gender identity, and in 2016 the US Department of Justice released guidelines forbidding corrections agencies from assigning trans inmates to men's or women's units solely on birth anatomy. In 2018 the Federal Bureau of Prisons revised its Transgender Offender Manual the other direction - deleting the sentence that the Transgender Executive Council 'will recommend housing by gender identity when appropriate' and instead making placement 'a case-by-case basis' in which 'biological sex' is 'the initial determination', with gender identity used only 'in rare cases'. No Delaware- or Maryland-specific placement policy is covered. Article last revised 2026-06-12; accessed 2026-10-04.

records.current_summary:
This state is one of the most legally protective in the country: its health-equity act, effective January 2024, mandates public-insurance coverage of gender-affirming treatment (hormones, puberty blockers and surgery) for an estimated 94,000 trans residents, tens of thousands, with the July 2026 national risk map counting that coverage among the country's most protective.

Protective law has not produced safety: an overlay of national monitoring records several hundred confirmed killings of trans women countrywide since 2008, a conservative undercount, and puts this state among the highest per-capita rates, and in 2026 two Black trans women were fatally shot in this state's largest city ten weeks apart, the most recent in September 2026, with the perpetrator still at large. Visitors should weigh the protections against that violence data.

prison_adds.title: Transgender rights in the United States (Wikipedia)
prison_adds.summary: Wikipedia's US transgender-rights article documents the nationally reported experience of trans women held in men's facilities, including the V-coding practice of assigning trans women to aggressive cisgender male cellmates ('a central part of a trans woman's sentence'), and reports that trans women who physically resist sexual assault are often criminally charged with assault and placed in solitary confinement, with the charge then used to extend the sentence and deny parole. A 2021 California study cited in the article found 69% of surveyed trans women prisoners reported being made to perform unwanted sexual acts, 58.5% reported violent sexual assault, and 88% reported a 'marriage-like relationship'. The article records no Maryland-specific placement rule, special unit, or named case. Article last revised 2026-10-04; accessed 2026-10-04.

records.current_summary:
In December 2024 this province enacted a package of three laws affecting transgender people as a class: school rules requiring parental notification and consent before staff use a student's gender-related chosen name or pronouns; a prohibition on puberty blockers and hormone therapy for minors; and related vital-statistics amendments. Trans and intersex advocacy organisations said at the time they would continue legal action.

In December 2025 the government invoked the constitutional override clause to shield all three laws from judicial remedy. Two national 2SLGBTQ+ organisations, together with five gender-diverse young people, say the constitutional challenge continues despite the shield - a provincial posture of legislating trans-targeting rules and then placing them beyond the courts.

prison_adds.title: Transgender rights in Canada (Wikipedia)
prison_adds.summary: Federal placement mechanics that govern trans prisoners in federal custody inside Alberta: since 2018, federal corrections operations accommodate offenders based on gender identity rather than sex assigned at birth, and the Correctional Service of Canada (CSC) permits gender-diverse offenders to request placement or transfer to a men's or women's institution aligned with their gender identity or expression, regardless of anatomy or the sex/gender marker on identity documents, with requests refused only where CSC finds unresolvable 'overriding health or safety concerns'. As of 2025 CSC reported 90 self-identified transgender women in federal institutions - 73 housed in men's institutions and 17 in women's. The Office of the Correctional Investigator called CSC's 2022 gender-diversity policy an important change but flagged the lack of clear parameters for what counts as an 'overriding health or safety concern' and the absence of a dedicated mechanism for gender-diverse prisoners to report abuse; provincial correctional policies vary and the article documents no Alberta-specific rule.

prison_adds.title: Danielle Smith (Wikipedia)
prison_adds.summary: Wikipedia biography of Alberta Premier Danielle Smith records her 12 February 2024 announcement of the province's package of trans-restricting measures (ban on gender-affirming care for minors, parental-consent rules for school pronouns and sexuality instruction, ban on trans women in women's sports), and that the bans 'would not include a ban on women's shelters, women's prisons or women's changing rooms', citing CBC's Lily Dupuis (12 April 2024) that Alberta's proposed transgender rules won't include public change rooms or jails. Outcome for the prison axis: Alberta's statutory trans package deliberately excluded jail and prison settings, so no provincial placement-by-birth-sex rule for trans prisoners was enacted, and no Alberta-specific trans-prisoner placement, special unit, or segregation case is documented.

records.current_summary:
In August 2023 the provincial government announced school policies requiring parents to be asked for permission before staff use a student's preferred name or pronouns (for pupils under 16), parents to be informed about the sexual-health curriculum, and third-party school programs to be paused. The province's senior trial court struck the rule down as unconstitutional; the government responded by legislating the consent rule into the Education Act and invoking the notwithstanding clause to immunise it from judicial review.

The matter went to the province's Court of Appeal, which largely allowed the government's appeal in August 2025; a current-status verification found no later ruling, leaving the re-legislated, shielded policy standing. For a visitor the education rule is primarily resident-facing; the durable signal is institutional: a provincial government re-legislating a policy a court had voided and shielding that from rights review - official hostility hardened past ordinary litigation.

prison_adds.title: Transgender rights in Canada (Wikipedia)
prison_adds.summary: Federal placement policy applicable to trans prisoners in federal custody inside Saskatchewan: since 2018 the Correctional Service of Canada accommodates offenders based on gender identity rather than sex assigned at birth and permits gender-diverse offenders to request placement in a men's or women's institution aligned with their gender identity or expression regardless of anatomy or identity-document sex/gender marker, refusing requests individually only where 'overriding health or safety concerns' cannot be resolved; as of 2025, of 90 self-identified transgender women in federal custody, 73 were housed in men's institutions and 17 in women's. The Office of the Correctional Investigator (2022-23 report) welcomed the 2022 gender-diversity policy but flagged unclear override parameters and the absence of a dedicated mechanism for gender-diverse prisoners to report abuse; provincial correctional policies vary (the article's only provincial example is Ontario) and no Saskatchewan-specific rule or case is documented in this source.

records.current_summary:
The state's principal international LGBT-rights federation's annual country review (February 2025) finds a troubling increase in the number and geographic spread of bias-motivated violence against LGBTI people, with incidents reported almost monthly - and includes in that finding a March 2025 scooter-mounted homophobic assault on a young man in this region's largest metropolitan periphery.

In October 2025 at a commuter railway station in the region's main metropolitan area an activist - president of a local LGBT association - was subjected to an escalating verbal homophobic attack ending in threats of stabbing by two young men. The station setting is one any visitor could occupy. The underlying local-newspaper report was bot-blocked at fetch time; it is retained as a sourced event on the strength of the recorded claim.

prison_adds.title: LGBTQ people in prison — Italy section (Wikipedia)
prison_adds.summary: Wikipedia 'LGBTQ people in prison' (Italy section, article revision 22 Sep 2026): in 2010 it was reported that Italy was to open its first dedicated transgender prison at Pozzale (Tuscany), a decision welcomed by gay-rights groups; as of 2013 the prison had not been created. This is the only documented Italian special-unit initiative for trans prisoners — announced, never opened — meaning trans detainees remain within the ordinary men's/women's prison circuit.

prison_adds.title: Italy 'to open first prison for transgender inmates' | BBC News
prison_adds.summary: BBC News (Jan 2010): Italy announced it would open one of the world's first prisons dedicated to transgender inmates at Pozzale, near Florence (Tuscany), converting an almost empty medium-security prison to house trans inmates mainly convicted of drug-related offences and prostitution; Italian gay-rights groups welcomed the move. The plan was never realized (per 2013 reporting), so no dedicated trans facility exists and trans prisoners continue to be placed in ordinary facilities.
